work.title: The Life and Death of King Richard the Second
work.author: William Shakespeare

scene.label: Act 3, Scene 4
scene.title: SCENE IV. Langley. The Duke of York's garden.
scene.location: Langley. The Duke of York's garden.

content.text: Enter the Queen and two Ladies.

lines.text: What sport shall we devise here in this garden
lines.plainText: What sport shall we devise here in this garden

lines.text: To drive away the heavy thought of care?
lines.plainText: To drive away the heavy thought of care

lines.text: Madam, we'll play at bowls.
lines.plainText: Madam we'll play at bowls

lines.text: 'Twill make me think the world is full of rubs
lines.plainText: 'Twill make me think the world is full of rubs

lines.text: And that my fortune runs against the bias.
lines.plainText: And that my fortune runs against the bias

lines.text: Madam, we'll dance.
lines.plainText: Madam we'll dance

lines.text: My legs can keep no measure in delight
lines.plainText: My legs can keep no measure in delight

lines.text: When my poor heart no measure keeps in grief.
lines.plainText: When my poor heart no measure keeps in grief

lines.text: Therefore no dancing, girl; some other sport.
lines.plainText: Therefore no dancing girl some other sport

lines.text: Madam, we'll tell tales.
lines.plainText: Madam we'll tell tales

lines.text: Of sorrow or of joy?
lines.plainText: Of sorrow or of joy

lines.text: Of either, madam.
lines.plainText: Of either madam

lines.text: Of neither, girl.
lines.plainText: Of neither girl

lines.text: For if of joy, being altogether wanting,
lines.plainText: For if of joy being altogether wanting

lines.text: It doth remember me the more of sorrow;
lines.plainText: It doth remember me the more of sorrow

lines.text: Or if of grief, being altogether had,
lines.plainText: Or if of grief being altogether had

lines.text: It adds more sorrow to my want of joy.
lines.plainText: It adds more sorrow to my want of joy

lines.text: For what I have I need not to repeat,
lines.plainText: For what I have I need not to repeat

lines.text: And what I want it boots not to complain.
lines.plainText: And what I want it boots not to complain

lines.text: Madam, I'll sing.
lines.plainText: Madam I'll sing

lines.text: 'Tis well that thou hast cause;
lines.plainText: 'Tis well that thou hast cause

lines.text: But thou shouldst please me better wouldst thou weep.
lines.plainText: But thou shouldst please me better wouldst thou weep

lines.text: I could weep, madam, would it do you good.
lines.plainText: I could weep madam would it do you good

lines.text: And I could sing, would weeping do me good,
lines.plainText: And I could sing would weeping do me good

lines.text: And never borrow any tear of thee.
lines.plainText: And never borrow any tear of thee

lines.text: But stay, here come the gardeners.
lines.plainText: But stay here come the gardeners

lines.text: Let's step into the shadow of these trees.
lines.plainText: Let's step into the shadow of these trees

lines.text: My wretchedness unto a row of pins,
lines.plainText: My wretchedness unto a row of pins

lines.text: They will talk of state, for everyone doth so
lines.plainText: They will talk of state for everyone doth so

lines.text: Against a change; woe is forerun with woe.
lines.plainText: Against a change woe is forerun with woe

content.text: Enter a Gardener and two Servants.

lines.text: Go, bind thou up young dangling apricocks,
lines.plainText: Go bind thou up young dangling apricocks

lines.text: Which, like unruly children, make their sire
lines.plainText: Which like unruly children make their sire

lines.text: Stoop with oppression of their prodigal weight.
lines.plainText: Stoop with oppression of their prodigal weight

lines.text: Give some supportance to the bending twigs.
lines.plainText: Give some supportance to the bending twigs

lines.text: Go thou, and like an executioner
lines.plainText: Go thou and like an executioner

lines.text: Cut off the heads of too fast-growing sprays
lines.plainText: Cut off the heads of too fastgrowing sprays

lines.text: That look too lofty in our commonwealth.
lines.plainText: That look too lofty in our commonwealth

lines.text: All must be even in our government.
lines.plainText: All must be even in our government

lines.text: You thus employed, I will go root away
lines.plainText: You thus employed I will go root away

lines.text: The noisome weeds which without profit suck
lines.plainText: The noisome weeds which without profit suck

lines.text: The soil's fertility from wholesome flowers.
lines.plainText: The soil's fertility from wholesome flowers

lines.text: Why should we in the compass of a pale
lines.plainText: Why should we in the compass of a pale

lines.text: Keep law and form and due proportion,
lines.plainText: Keep law and form and due proportion

lines.text: Showing, as in a model, our firm estate,
lines.plainText: Showing as in a model our firm estate

lines.text: When our sea-walled garden, the whole land,
lines.plainText: When our seawalled garden the whole land

lines.text: Is full of weeds, her fairest flowers choked up,
lines.plainText: Is full of weeds her fairest flowers choked up

lines.text: Her fruit trees all unpruned, her hedges ruined,
lines.plainText: Her fruit trees all unpruned her hedges ruined

lines.text: Her knots disordered, and her wholesome herbs
lines.plainText: Her knots disordered and her wholesome herbs

lines.text: Swarming with caterpillars?
lines.plainText: Swarming with caterpillars

lines.text: Hold thy peace.
lines.plainText: Hold thy peace

lines.text: He that hath suffered this disordered spring
lines.plainText: He that hath suffered this disordered spring

lines.text: Hath now himself met with the fall of leaf.
lines.plainText: Hath now himself met with the fall of leaf

lines.text: The weeds which his broad-spreading leaves did shelter,
lines.plainText: The weeds which his broadspreading leaves did shelter

lines.text: That seemed in eating him to hold him up,
lines.plainText: That seemed in eating him to hold him up

lines.text: Are plucked up, root and all, by Bolingbroke—
lines.plainText: Are plucked up root and all by Bolingbroke

lines.text: I mean the Earl of Wiltshire, Bushy, Green.
lines.plainText: I mean the Earl of Wiltshire Bushy Green

lines.text: What, are they dead?
lines.plainText: What are they dead

lines.text: They are. And Bolingbroke
lines.plainText: They are And Bolingbroke

lines.text: Hath seized the wasteful King. O, what pity is it
lines.plainText: Hath seized the wasteful King O what pity is it

lines.text: That he had not so trimmed and dressed his land
lines.plainText: That he had not so trimmed and dressed his land

lines.text: As we this garden! We at time of year
lines.plainText: As we this garden We at time of year

lines.text: Do wound the bark, the skin of our fruit trees,
lines.plainText: Do wound the bark the skin of our fruit trees

lines.text: Lest, being over-proud in sap and blood,
lines.plainText: Lest being overproud in sap and blood

lines.text: With too much riches it confound itself.
lines.plainText: With too much riches it confound itself

lines.text: Had he done so to great and growing men,
lines.plainText: Had he done so to great and growing men

lines.text: They might have lived to bear and he to taste
lines.plainText: They might have lived to bear and he to taste

lines.text: Their fruits of duty. Superfluous branches
lines.plainText: Their fruits of duty Superfluous branches

lines.text: We lop away, that bearing boughs may live.
lines.plainText: We lop away that bearing boughs may live

lines.text: Had he done so, himself had home the crown,
lines.plainText: Had he done so himself had home the crown

lines.text: Which waste of idle hours hath quite thrown down.
lines.plainText: Which waste of idle hours hath quite thrown down

lines.text: What, think you the King shall be deposed?
lines.plainText: What think you the King shall be deposed

lines.text: Depressed he is already, and deposed
lines.plainText: Depressed he is already and deposed

lines.text: 'Tis doubt he will be. Letters came last night
lines.plainText: 'Tis doubt he will be Letters came last night

lines.text: To a dear friend of the good Duke of York's
lines.plainText: To a dear friend of the good Duke of York's

lines.text: That tell black tidings.
lines.plainText: That tell black tidings

lines.text: O, I am pressed to death through want of speaking!
lines.plainText: O I am pressed to death through want of speaking

lines.text: Pardon me, madam. Little joy have I
lines.plainText: Pardon me madam Little joy have I

lines.text: To breathe this news; yet what I say is true.
lines.plainText: To breathe this news yet what I say is true

lines.text: King Richard, he is in the mighty hold
lines.plainText: King Richard he is in the mighty hold

lines.text: Of Bolingbroke. Their fortunes both are weighed.
lines.plainText: Of Bolingbroke Their fortunes both are weighed

lines.text: In your lord's scale is nothing but himself,
lines.plainText: In your lord's scale is nothing but himself

lines.text: And some few vanities that make him light;
lines.plainText: And some few vanities that make him light

lines.text: But in the balance of great Bolingbroke,
lines.plainText: But in the balance of great Bolingbroke

lines.text: Besides himself, are all the English peers,
lines.plainText: Besides himself are all the English peers

lines.text: And with that odds he weighs King Richard down.
lines.plainText: And with that odds he weighs King Richard down

lines.text: Post you to London, and you will find it so.
lines.plainText: Post you to London and you will find it so

lines.text: I speak no more than everyone doth know.
lines.plainText: I speak no more than everyone doth know

lines.text: Nimble mischance, that art so light of foot,
lines.plainText: Nimble mischance that art so light of foot

lines.text: Doth not thy embassage belong to me,
lines.plainText: Doth not thy embassage belong to me

lines.text: And am I last that knows it? O, thou thinkest
lines.plainText: And am I last that knows it O thou thinkest

lines.text: To serve me last that I may longest keep
lines.plainText: To serve me last that I may longest keep

lines.text: Thy sorrow in my breast. Come, ladies, go
lines.plainText: Thy sorrow in my breast Come ladies go

lines.text: To meet at London London's king in woe.
lines.plainText: To meet at London London's king in woe

lines.text: What, was I born to this, that my sad look
lines.plainText: What was I born to this that my sad look

lines.text: Should grace the triumph of great Bolingbroke?
lines.plainText: Should grace the triumph of great Bolingbroke

lines.text: Gard'ner, for telling me these news of woe,
lines.plainText: Gard'ner for telling me these news of woe

lines.text: Pray God the plants thou graft'st may never grow!
lines.plainText: Pray God the plants thou graft'st may never grow

lines.text: Poor Queen, so that thy state might be no worse,
lines.plainText: Poor Queen so that thy state might be no worse

lines.text: I would my skill were subject to thy curse.
lines.plainText: I would my skill were subject to thy curse

lines.text: Here did she fall a tear. Here in this place
lines.plainText: Here did she fall a tear Here in this place

lines.text: I'll set a bank of rue, sour herb of grace.
lines.plainText: I'll set a bank of rue sour herb of grace

lines.text: Rue even for ruth here shortly shall be seen
lines.plainText: Rue even for ruth here shortly shall be seen

lines.text: In the remembrance of a weeping queen.
lines.plainText: In the remembrance of a weeping queen
